status: draft, not checked by a clinician
note: Standalone guideline search questions for Phase 2B, drafted from the Uganda guidelines on 2026-11-25. Each question is worded as a clinician would ask it, without the passage's own wording; each gold quote is copied from the file (table code included) and checked to be in it. The search should return a gold passage.

questions.question: How often should I repeat a viral load test in an adult who has been on treatment for over a year and is doing well?

gold.quote: The second VL following the first suppressed viral load should be done at 12 months after initiation of ART and thereafter every 12 months if it is suppressed.

questions.question: How frequently do I need to check kidney function in a patient who has been taking tenofovir for years?

gold.quote: eGFR for experienced patient on TDF every 12 months

questions.question: Which patients should get cholesterol and sugar tests at a routine visit?

gold.quote: Lipid profile and blood glucoseIf PLHIV has comorbidities (diabetes mellitus, hypertension) or lifestyle risk factors or on ART for more than five years or is ≥ 45 years

questions.question: A patient on the standard once-daily combination complains of back pain, bone aches and passing less urine. Which of his drugs is likely responsible?

gold.quote: Chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury and Fanconi syndrome Decreased bone mineral density Lactic acidosis or severe Hepatomegaly with steatosisLower back pain, change in urine volume Bone aches, spontaneous fractures

questions.question: My patient on the older non-nucleoside regimen has vivid nightmares and low mood. What should I do about the regimen?

gold.quote: Dizziness, insomnia, abnormal dreams, or mental symptoms (anxiety, depression, mental confusion, suicidality) New-onset seizures
Reassure, If symptoms persist, substitute EFV with DTG or LPV/r (if appropriate DTG formulation is not available)

questions.question: A patient on the dolutegravir regimen cannot sleep at night. What do I advise?

gold.quote: Insomnia: Ensure patient is taking DTG during the day if it persists then substitute with EFV

questions.question: Is it safe to keep a patient on the dolutegravir regimen if he is also put on an older epilepsy medicine?

gold.quote: Carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30-70%Use valproic acid

questions.question: My patient takes antacids and iron tablets every day. How should I time his dolutegravir?

gold.quote: Reduce DTG levelsUse DTG 2 hours before or 6 hours after the prod-uct to avoid interaction

questions.question: A patient on a boosted protease inhibitor needs a cholesterol-lowering tablet. What should I prescribe?

gold.quote: Simvastatin, rosuvastatin, atorvastatinATV/r, LPV/r, DRV and RTVInhibition of CYP450 3A4 (reduced metabolism of statins)Use atorvastatin with lowered dose and monitor for side effects like muscle pains

questions.question: A patient developed itching, faintness and breathlessness soon after starting abacavir. Which drug do I swap it for?

gold.quote: Hypersensitivity reactionSkin itching (localized or diffuse) dizziness, faintness, difficulty breathing, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, and abdominal crampingSubstitute with TDF If TDF is contraindicated: substitute with AZT

questions.question: A diabetic adult is due to be moved to the dolutegravir regimen. Is that acceptable, and if not what do I give?

gold.quote: Known diabetics should not be initiated or transitioned to DTG. Give an EFV400 or an ATV/r-based regimen.

questions.question: Which first-line regimen do I choose for an adult whose kidney filtration rate is low?

gold.quote: Adults and adolescents eligible for DTG should only be initiated on ABC+3TC+DTG if TDF is contraindicated (Table 74), including the following conditions:
Kidney disease and estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) below 60 ml/min.

questions.question: Which treatment regimen should I start in a woman newly found HIV positive at her first antenatal visit?

gold.quote: Newly diagnosed HIV-infected pregnant and breastfeeding women will be initiated on Tenofovir tenofovir alefenamide, Lamivudine and Dolutegravir (TDF+ 3TC + DTG or TAF + FTC + DTG).

questions.question: A pregnant woman is stable and suppressed on the efavirenz-based regimen. Should I switch her now?

gold.quote: If already on TDF or TAF +3TC+EFV and stable with suppressed VL, maintain on TDF or TAF +3TC+EFV400 until 6-9 months postpartum and then transition to TDF or TAF +3TC+DTG if VL within past 6 months is suppressed.

questions.question: How often do I check the viral load of a pregnant woman who is already suppressed on treatment?

gold.quote: If VL is supressed repeat VL every 3 months throughout pregnancy until cessation of breastfeeding.

questions.question: A patient on the dolutegravir regimen is starting rifampicin for TB. Does the ARV dose need to change?

gold.quote: Rifampicin lowers DTG levelsAdjust DTG dose to twice daily

questions.question: When should I begin ARVs in a newly diagnosed patient who has just started TB drugs?

gold.quote: ART should be started as soon as possible within two weeks of initiating TB treatment, regardless of CD4 cell count, among people living with HIV (Except when signs and symptoms of meningitis are present)

questions.question: What ARV backbone should a patient who also has chronic hepatitis B receive?

gold.quote: Treatment of HBV/HIV co-infected personInitiate ART with TDF or TAF -containing regimen.

questions.question: A patient's viral load came back high. How soon should I see him for the first adherence session?

gold.quote: Conduct a first intensive adherence counselling within 7-30 days of result return.

questions.question: How many adherence counselling sessions must a patient with a detectable viral load complete before we consider a resistance test?

gold.quote: The patient should have had three intensified adherence counseling sessions one month apart after the initial detectable viral load.
